newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Valora sees sales of four bln Sfr in 2002.
newsitem.headline: Valora sees sales of four bln Sfr in 2002.

text.p: Swiss-based retail group Valora Holding AG said it was planning for annual turnover of around four billion Swiss francs in year 2002 and sales each year are expected to increase by an average 10 percent, including acquisitions.

Based on a targeted operating profit (EBIT) margin of six percent and a net margin of four percent, designated Rete Hartmann also told a news conference that this should result in operating profit of 240 million Swiss francs and a net profit of 160 million.
In 1996 Valora's turnover rose to 2.9 billion francs from 2.87 billion and net profit jumped to 72.1 million from 41.2 million.
Hartmann also told a news conference that the company also wanted to achieve organic growth above the industry average.
Chairman Georg Krneta said he did not expect Valora this year to reach the 1994 record net profit of 98.5 million francs, but possibly in 1998.
Initially, however, the group will have to digest the effects of the recent spin-off of the previous company unit Selecta, which went public this year.
